A constant temperature difference of 6.7°C (12°F) was assumed, corresponding to the campus design supply temperature of 42°F (5.56°C) and return temperature of 54°F (12.22°C). This assumption is conservative during low cooling demand periods, as variable frequency drives can reduce pump flow while maintaining the desired ΔT, thereby lowering energy use. At high loads, flow rates increased to meet the loads, while the system was assumed to maintain the consistent ∆𝑇, representing an idealized but balanced estimate for techno-economic comparison. The calculated hourly-varying flow rates were then incorporated into the frictional losses and reservoir pressure drop calculations for hourly pumping power (kW). Using the time-of-use rates discussed earlier in Section 2.4.2, annual pumping costs of the single-doublet and two-doublet systems were estimated at $52,700 and $26,360, respectively. While GeoSWAC’s pumping costs may be higher due to the need for groundwater circulation (compared to $11,815 per year in the chiller-based case), the overall operational cost is significantly lower due to the avoidance of energy-intensive chillers and evaporative water losses. Particularly, when the water cost of $241,193/year is considered as avoided operational cost, the net operational cost for GeoSWAC becomes negative, estimated at −$188,492 for a single-doublet system and −$214,832 for a two-doublet system. However, operational and maintenance costs associated with water chemistry effects, including scaling, corrosion, and material degradation due to thermal cycling, are not explicitly included in this analysis and represent an important consideration for future site-specific design and economic assessment. 4.2.4 Levelized Cost of Cooling The LCOC of GeoSWAC with the two configurations was calculated using the following parameters: a 20-year system lifetime, 5% discount rate, and an annual cooling energy output of 19.1 GWh. Capital costs were estimated at $2.1 million for the single-doublet system and $2.9 million for the two-doublet system (Table 3). Annual operational costs were $52,702 and $26,361, respectively, which were significantly lower than $390,946 for the chiller-based scenario. The resulting LCOC values for GeoSWAC were $11.1/MWh (single) and $13.1/MWh (double), GeoSWAC achieved a lower LCOC than chiller-based systems ($30.2/MWh compared to $33.6/MWh), primarily due to much lower electricity consumption and the elimination of water losses. While the capital cost for GeoSWAC was 11%–14% lower than that of chiller- based systems, the operational cost of GeoSWAC was approximately 90% lower on average, resulting in an overall LCOC reduction of 62%.
